name: What storage changes help when two people are always bumping into each other in the kitchen?

mainEntity.name: What storage changes help when two people are always bumping into each other in the kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: If two or more people cook together, storage should support separate work zones and prevent doors or drawers from competing for the same space. Pots and utensils belong near the cooking area, prep tools near the main counter, and dishes near cleanup or serving areas. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design can review circulation and storage together when developing a kitchen layout. More cabinets do not solve conflicts if the work aisle is narrow or appliance doors collide. Key factors: number of cooks; counter locations; appliance placement; door and drawer clearances. Practical guidance: Describe where each person stands during meal preparation and cleanup. Test proposed storage against open-door conditions, not only a closed-room drawing. Keep the most frequently shared tools in neutral, easy-access locations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Improve zones and clearances rather than simply adding cabinets. Separate cooking, prep, and cleanup storage, review appliance and drawer conflicts, and show how the layout works with doors and drawers fully open.
